aboutMe:
I’m Dr. Craig Filipkowski and have been in education as a teacher, administrator, and/or consultant since 2000. I was recently trained by Dr. Michael Marquardt for Action Learning in Washington D.C., who is one of the world’s “thought leaders” in this particular intervention.
The intervention has 2 objectives:
solve real world problems,
develop learners and leaders
Presently, I’m practicing this coaching skill in preparation for my research dissertation that will highlight the impact of Action Learning teams on leadership development and solving problems simultaneously.
I’m doing all the work pro bono and would love to work with P-12 educators around the Cincinnati, Ohio area. These clients must be interested in developing their leadership skills while solving real and relevant problems in a team based format.
Even though Action Learning is frequently implemented as a tool in business organizations such as GE, Boeing, and Caterpillar, it has also been used in P-12 education. I’m specifically interested in education because of my training but more importantly my duty to give back in local communities.
What complex issues are you facing that have you perplexed?
…influx of ELL students? ...how do we approach career and college readiness as a building? ...as a district? ...disengaged learners? ...mental health needs/concerns?
I can provide structure to specified meetings that will enable you to get the most out of your staff and toward solving important problems.
Rather than just offering ideas on how to solve problems and buy into my own strategy, I spend energy on getting people to share and explore their own ideas as a team.
My focus on action learning will provide you with 2 outcomes: action toward solving the problem and learning on several levels (individual, team, and organizational).

name: Gemma van Steekelenburg
title: Ms.
aboutMe:
‘Het is mijn passie mensen bewust te maken hoe harde en zachte skills in werk en privé verweven zijn en ons op allerlei manieren beïnvloeden. JA het gaat in het werk om targets, processen en nog veel meer praktische zaken. En er is meer!
Gemma van Steekelenburg weet wat het is om vast te zitten in een patroon of groef. Hoe je jezelf in de maling kunt nemen om niet dát te gaan doen wat eigenlijk wel goed zou zijn. Zij is zichzelf regelmatig tegengekomen (en soms nog hoor :)). Zij is in 2006 met alles anderZ gestart, na een eerdere ondernemerservaring en vele jaren bij verschillende organisaties in dienst. Het belangrijkste wat zij als collega en medewerker inbracht was aandacht geven, doorvragen en creatieve oplossingen aanbrengen. Hiermee doorgaand voor zichzelf vanaf 2006 zorgde al snel dat de ene na de andere klus over haar heen buitelde en dit binnen zeer uiteenlopende werkvelden. Dit leidde ertoe dat het Gemma steeds meer energie kostte, teveel energie. Het werd tijd voor persoonlijke aandacht en keuzes. Een proces van grondige persoonlijke ontwikkeling volgde en een aantal klanten moesten het veld ruimen. De aandacht, creativiteit en het doorvragen bleven en was nu onderbouwd met een flinke bak aan kennis van hoe patronen en groeven gedrag beïnvloeden. En een flinke bak aan oerkracht.

Dit is hoe zij er nu in staat; Gemma houdt van ruimte en doen wat energie geeft. Ze is bij voorkeur buiten in de natuur en coacht en traint daar teams en managers die vanuit balans in hoofd, hart en handen willen werken en managen. Ze gaat aan de slag met het gehele systeem, wat er boven én onder water zit, dichtbij staat en verder weg ligt. Dat gaat ook over voelen en ervaren en de controle vastpakken en ook loslaten (en ook dat leert ze je). Dat is anderZ dan anders; met je hoofd erbij maar ook met je lijf en vooral doen.

En tja... Soms komen er dan dingen bovendrijven waar we het vooral niet over willen hebben. Met haar goed gevulde gereedschapskist, humor en open prikkelende vragen (eventueel met hier of daar een paard), coacht ze je via ongebruikelijke routes hier dwars doorheen. Het gaat er toch over, blijft een veilig proces en zo creëert zij ruimte voor een nieuwe stip op de horizon . Met welk gereedschap dan? O.a. met Systemisch werk , Deep Democracy, Action Learning , Rake Vragen , Communicatiestijlen, TMA en Paardencoaching.

Gemma over ’Controle over’ ; Wij mensen denken dat we controle hebben over bijna alles wat we doen. Dat we lastige situaties met onze ratio kunnen oplossen. Wij zijn echter ook een diersoort. Met nog best veel bijbehorende dierlijke instincten en dito overlevingsdrang. Tel hier onze ingesleten patronen bij op en je beseft dat ‘controle over’ een stuk minder vanzelfsprekend is. Door jezelf min of meer bewust ‘live in actie’ te ervaren wordt je je bewust van je onbewuste en krijgt ‘controle over’ een nieuwe betekenis. Ik daag je uit, probeer het eens!’

To keep thriving we must keep learning, tackling these challenges with fresh perspectives, while staying connected to what gives us energy and meaning. Our transformative experiences enable people to do just that. Experiences are Learning-led, Engagement-led or a combination of both – helping people perform effectively in a complex world. We partner with companies across the world, to bring out the best in their people through these transformative experiences using a customised approach based on core principles of: - Staying Curious. - Designing for Impact. - Extending & Extending Trust. - Leading with Humanity Work is usually focused on People Development, Organizational Development, Team Development, Organizational Development, Employee Engagement, Corporate Volunteering and Community Impact. aboutMe:
Dr. Michael Marquardt is Professor Emeritus of Human Resource Development and International Affairs at George Washington University. He was a co-founder and first President of the World Institute for Action Learning (WIAL), and now serves as a member of the WIAL Global Advisory Committee.

Mike has held a number of senior management, training and marketing positions with organizations such as Grolier, American Society for Training and Development, Association Management, Overseas Education Fund, TradeTec, and U.S. Office of Personnel Management. Dr. Marquardt has trained more than 100,000 managers in nearly 150 countries since beginning his international experience in Spain in 1969. Consulting assignments have included Marriott, Microsoft, Sony Music, Goodrich, Motorola, Nortel, Alcoa, Boeing, Caterpillar, United Nations Development Program, Xerox, Nokia, Constellation, Samsung, Organization of American States, and Singapore Airlines as well as the governments of Indonesia, Laos, Ethiopia, Zambia, Egypt, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Russia, Jamaica, Honduras, and Swaziland.

Mike is the author of 26 books and over 100 professional articles in the fields of leadership, learning, globalization and organizational change including Action Learning for Developing Leaders and Organizations, Optimizing the Power of Action Learning, Leading with Questions, Building the Learning Organization (selected as Book of the Year by the Academy of HRD), The Global Advantage, Action Learning in Action, Global Leaders for the 21 st Century, Global Human Resource Development , Technology-Based Learning , and Global Teams . Over one million copies of his publications have been sold in nearly a dozen languages worldwide. Dr. Marquardt also served as the Editor of the UNESCO Encyclopedia volume on Human Resources and is an editor and/or advisor for several leading professional journals around the world. He has been a keynote speaker at international conferences in Australia, Japan, Philippines, Malaysia, South Africa, Singapore, and India as well as throughout North America.

Dr. Marquardt's achievements and leadership have been recognized though numerous awards including the International Practitioner of the Year Award from the American Society for Training and Development and the Scholar of the Year Award from the Academy of Human Resource Development. His writings and accomplishments in action learning have earned him honorary doctoral degrees from universities in Asia, Europe and North America.

He received his doctorate in Human Resource Development from George Washington University and his Masters and Bachelor Degrees from Maryknoll College. Dr. Marquardt has done graduate work at Harvard, Columbia and the University of Virginia. He enjoys skiing, folk music and traveling with his Swiss wife, four children and ten grandchildren.

I believe that action learning is a powerful tool which enhances personal effectiveness, leadership and self-confidence. My application of this tool within classrooms and among existing teams has enabled me to observe the development of collaborative teams and enhanced team performance. The process encourages equal participation, improves self-awareness and is effective in helping individuals to identify the real problem and to create solution-based strategies which are both innovative and effective. I am currently in the process of researching how action learning can help to develop interprofessional collaborative skills among university students. Creating positive, respectful teams, encouraging equal participation and teaching individuals to reinforce participation and build on other's ideas provides the foundation for creating collaborative, innovative, interprofessional teams.
Among my career accomplishments, I have become an ethics champion, serving on several ethical review committees and advocating the best possible researched based services. I have spearheaded the development of an annual conference and became an ACE provider, ensuring BCBA standards were maintained. I love creative problem solving and have applied these skills to my careers as clinical supervisor, senior therapist and behaviour consultant, for over 27 years. I am also a dynamic speaker and have presented at a number of conferences on topics such as motivation, inter-professional collaboration, anxiety, sexuality and development of a best practice model for providing community based behavioural services to adults.
I am a Board-Certified Behaviour Analyst (BCBA), a Certified Action Learning Coach and a long-standing member of the member of the Association for Behavior Analysis International (ABAI) and Ontario Association of Behaviour Analysts (ONTABA) and have served on a number of committees such as the ONTABA Jurisprudence Committee and the ONTABA conference committee. I am committed to sharing all of my many stories and the dissemination of applied behaviour analysis through interactive education, and mentorship of students in the field and research in socially significant issues. I feel the importance of creating compassionate clinicians who support diversity, equity and creating foundational skills in self-awareness and dismantling the systems of oppression which may impact their future clients. Integrating topics such as trauma informed care and interprofessional collaboration through experiential learning and action learning are some of my latest strategies. I feel passionate about expanding the field's reach into addressing world issues. I feel that we can make a difference and this world needs our help.

aboutMe:
Ravi VS, FFA (UK), FIPA (Australia)
Ravi VS is a Strategic Foresight Practitioner, Leadership Intelligence Advisor, Action Learning Coach, and Regenerative Systems Thinker with more than 38 years of international experience spanning 54 countries. Throughout his career, he has worked with governments, multinational corporations, higher education institutions, public sector organisations, and emerging enterprises to strengthen leadership capability, organisational preparedness, and strategic decision-making in an increasingly uncertain world.
His work integrates Strategic Foresight, Action Learning, systems thinking, decision intelligence, and regenerative leadership to help organisations move beyond reacting to change toward anticipating and shaping it. Ravi believes that leadership today is no longer defined by the ability to solve today's problems alone, but by the ability to recognise emerging signals, challenge assumptions, and make better decisions before disruption becomes a crisis.
As an executive advisor, facilitator, and educator, Ravi is recognised for helping leaders develop stronger judgement under uncertainty. Rather than focusing solely on trends, his work emphasises signal intelligence, structured inquiry, critical questioning, and evidence-based reflection—principles that closely align with the philosophy of Action Learning. He sees Action Learning and Strategic Foresight as complementary disciplines: Action Learning strengthens learning through questioning and reflection, while Strategic Foresight expands leadership capacity by preparing organisations for multiple possible futures.
Over the past three decades, Ravi has designed and applied practical leadership and organisational frameworks that integrate foresight, systems thinking, AI-enabled intelligence, and experiential learning. His work has supported leadership development, organisational transformation, workforce capability, governance, and national foresight initiatives across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
Ravi is also actively contributing to the emerging field of organisational preparedness. His research explores how organisations can strengthen their ability to anticipate, interpret, decide, adapt, and align in environments characterised by rapid technological change, geopolitical uncertainty, and AI-driven disruption. His work has been recognised internationally, including the acceptance of his research for presentation at the Futures Conference in Turku, Finland, one of the world's leading conferences on futures studies.
Passionate about developing future-ready leaders, Ravi continues to advocate for integrating Strategic Foresight, Action Learning, and regenerative thinking into leadership practice, organisational development, and management education.
About Invictus Leader
Founded in 1988 in Scotland, Invictus Leader Sdn. Bhd. is a Malaysian-based Strategic Foresight and Leadership Intelligence consultancy dedicated to helping organisations build long-term capability rather than short-term solutions. Over the past 38 years, the firm has partnered with more than 15,000 organisations across 54 countries, supporting governments, multinational corporations, universities, and SMEs in strengthening leadership, organisational preparedness, and strategic capability.
Invictus Leader specialises in helping organisations anticipate disruption, navigate uncertainty, and build resilience through the integration of Strategic Foresight, Action Learning, systems thinking, leadership development, and AI-enabled decision intelligence. Rather than delivering conventional consulting or training programmes, the firm works alongside clients to build internal capability that enables sustainable performance and continuous adaptation.
Core Areas of Practice
Strategic Foresight and Scenario Intelligence
Supporting organisations to identify emerging signals, explore alternative futures, and improve long-term strategic decision-making.
Leadership Intelligence and Organisational Preparedness
Developing leaders who can exercise sound judgement, think systemically, and lead confidently in complex, AI-augmented environments.
Action Learning and Capability Development
Partnering with organisations, universities, and public institutions to strengthen leadership capability through questioning insight, reflective practice, collaborative problem-solving, and experiential learning.
AI-Enabled Decision Intelligence
Combining AI-assisted environmental scanning with human judgement to improve strategic planning, workforce readiness, governance, and policy development.
Our Philosophy
At Invictus Leader, we believe that transformation alone is no longer sufficient in a world characterised by accelerating change. Organisations require the continuous infusion of new intelligence, fresh perspectives, and enhanced decision-making capability to remain relevant and resilient.
We describe this philosophy as Transfusion—the intentional integration of Strategic Foresight, Action Learning, regenerative thinking, and leadership intelligence to strengthen organisational preparedness and create sustainable value for the future.
